title: Recursive leaf-first recovery
story: I can finish incomplete work from its starting point without repeating completed effort.
jobStory: When related work is incomplete, I want to recover it from where it began, so I can finish the original task without repeating completed work.

scenarios.name: Recursive leaf-first recovery
scenarios.given: A user points to an incomplete root session with failed descendants.
scenarios.when: Recovery is started without the user supplying child IDs.
scenarios.then: Affected leaves finish first, their separate results propagate upward behind sibling barriers, and the root is reactivated after descendant work completes.

invalidation: A descendant is skipped despite failed work; sibling results are merged; a parent resumes before required siblings finish; completed work is repeated; or recovery stops without the root being reactivated.

items.description: Affected leaves finish first, their separate results propagate upward behind sibling barriers, and the root is reactivated after descendant work completes.
items.evidence: Observable session/tree state and a recorded recovery result; capture a screenshot or structured event when available. Evidence: docs/proof/f01v1-demo/ (attempt 9, 2026-11-09, root ses_e408c94f5ffewWj2xFGZsfC8z4, ACCEPTANCE PASS).

routine.reason: The user specified an ordered recovery routine; its contract is rendered in recursive-wake-up.md.
inputs: User-selected session ID (usually the root, but it may be any session in the tree)
Existing session-family relationships and current state of descendants
Work, messages, and results produced since the interruption
Failure information when available: timeout, internet connection drop, or provider-credit/credential problem
The intended model, subject to OpenCode controls

steps.description: Walk descendants to affected failed leaves without asking the user for child IDs.
Continue and finish each leaf’s work.
Prefer child-to-direct-parent wake with its own summary and brief note; otherwise collect output and pass it upward.
Preserve one attributable handoff per child.
Hold the parent until all required sibling recoveries complete.
Resolve children, resume each failed parent, and pass its result to its own parent until the root is reactivated.
Reuse completed/relaunched work and avoid duplicating the better existing investigation.
Account for timeout, connection, and provider-credit/credential failures under OpenCode controls; keep agents on the intended model.

skillDoc.reason: Human-readable recovery routine and ambiguity register.

provenance.quote:
for each leaf agent, i tell them 'continue and finish up'
we repeat until the root agent is reactivated

ambiguities: How to distinguish failed from slow or still-running sessions.
Which descendants are required participants in a sibling barrier.
Who coordinates and what mechanism it uses when a child cannot wake its parent.
Handoff payload schema, exact fields, summary length, and ordering; only a summary plus a brief note is specified.
Reconciliation authority when messages, journals, or files conflict, including how to compare competing investigations.
Termination meaning (root running, root task done, or every descendant verified).
Model/depth defaults beyond explicit pinModel behavior and model inheritance for sessions not resumed by this run.
Data-model schema and persistence.
Whether core-restart emulation belongs in this plugin.
What retry, wait, model-switch, or stop policy applies to each failure class (timeout, network drop, provider credits/creds)?
notes: The inventory combines two exact quote fragments from the same source message.

Verified 2026-11-09: F-01-V1 acceptance passed on attempt 9 (root ses_e408c94f5ffewWj2xFGZsfC8z4) — an exact 1/2/4 tree of 7 sessions was built and interrupted, tree.recover resumed all 7 with rootReactivated=true, all 6 handoffs were delivered with parentResumed=true, and every original session finished idle_outcome=succeeded with a recovery:done journal entry (descendant count still exactly 7). Adversarial verification PASSed against the primary artifacts. Evidence: docs/proof/f01v1-demo/.
Implementation status (2026-11-01): tree.recover implements the recursive routine and NRR discovery; adversarial/live verification passed 2026-11-09 on attempt 9 (see docs/proof/f01v1-demo/).

Coordinator scope: The specified steps describe the desired outcome and handoff preference, but do not specify coordinator implementation mechanics. Do not infer a payload schema, summary length, or coordination mechanism from “summary” and “brief note.”

Termination condition: The specified stopping point is: the root is reactivated with all descendants successfully finished. What “successfully finished” proves, and whether root reactivation is sufficient or the root’s task must also be complete, remain open questions. Do not claim the workflow is verified until that termination contract is resolved and observable proof passes.

Why this was lost: The failed build translated the requested workflow into five primitives—`whoami`, `family`, `journal`, `handoff`, and `wake`—but never implemented the crawler, the sibling barrier, or upward result bubbling. Those primitives do not by themselves satisfy the leaf-first recovery feature.

algorithm.text: Start from the session the user points to, usually any level and often the root, when it is incomplete.

provenance.quote: i come to a session (usually root, could be any level), i see that it didn't complete.

algorithm.text: Inspect the visible failure or failed sub-agent calls and recursively check for leaf agents.

provenance.quote: i usually see some error that killed it (internet, ai creds) or i see red sub agent calls (failed). i click into those, check recursively for the leaf agents.

algorithm.text: For each leaf agent, tell it to continue and finish up.

provenance.quote: 3. and for each leaf agent, i tell them "continue and finish up [and wake up your parent by injecting your summary into thier context with brief note about what happened to you]"

algorithm.text: Prefer for the leaf to wake its parent by injecting its own summary into the parent context with a brief note about what happened.

provenance.quote: wake up your parent by injecting your summary into thier context with brief note about what happened to you

algorithm.text: Alternatively, wait for the child to complete, collect its output, and give it to the parent.

provenance.quote: wait for the child to complete and then we have to grab the output and then we have to give it to the parent.

algorithm.text: Keep each child handoff separate so the parent can tell what each sub-agent did.

provenance.quote: I imagine that they keep it separate so that they can tell what each sub agent did.

algorithm.text: When multiple children failed, wait for both before letting the parent get cooking.

provenance.quote: especially if multiple failed, because then we would have to Wait for both of those children before we really want the parent to get cooking or whatever.

algorithm.text: Let the parent know that recovery of its children is underway.

provenance.quote: We want the parent to know that we are finishing their children.

algorithm.text: Prefer leaf wake-up so that the parents are then woken recursively as each child finishes and passes its work upward.

provenance.quote: preferably we wake up the leaf and then that will recursively wake up the parents whenever each child finishes and they will pass their stuff to the parent.

algorithm.text: Repeat until the root is reactivated with all descendants successfully finished.

provenance.quote: we repeat until the root agent is reactivated, with all descendants having successfully finished.

algorithm.text: Account for what happened since the chain died and avoid duplicating effort or results.

provenance.quote: time and turns - knowing what happened since the sub agent chain died, and respecting it/not duplicating effort or results.

algorithm.text: When existing investigations compete, recognize that deciding who did the work/investigation better may be necessary.

provenance.quote: then its a question of who did the work/investigation better

algorithm.text: Account for behavior differences across timeout, internet-drop, and provider-credential errors under OpenCode controls.

provenance.quote: the diff in behavior from timeout, internet drop, open ai creds, with the diff types of errors, and agent-tree behavior based on those (oc controls)

algorithm.text: Pin all agents involved, including orchestrators, to the intended model.

provenance.quote: beware you must pin all agents involved to your own model, and orchs must do the same.

story: I can recover only the latest batch of work inside an orchestrator, leaving superseded sub-agent attempts dead.

ambiguities: How should an excluded node with live (running) children be treated?
Should exclusion apply to running nodes or only failed/interrupted/unknown?
notes: Exclusion applies to nodes classified failed, interrupted, or unknown: they are recorded as skipped-superseded and count as already-complete for barrier purposes. Excluded succeeded nodes already fall through the already-complete branch; excluded running nodes stay pending (conservative — they are not silently marked complete).
An excluded node is barrier-satisfying even when its own children remain unresolved, so a superseded batch cannot deadlock the parent that outlived it.
